patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` applied cleanly in the reused workspace and changes the exact `fwupd_guid_from_string()` section-length guard from `&&` to `||`. On the original staged witness, the fixed original still reaches `guid_section_guard` with `strlen(split[4]) == 5` but leaves `guid_tail_copy` absent, so the repaired guard blocks the unsafe tail-copy path. The closest source-grounded perturbation, `same_digits_valid_guid`, keeps the same 32 hex digits and only redistributes the dashes to a valid `8-4-4-4-12` layout; that case reaches `guid_tail_copy` genuinely on the fixed side with `strlen(split[4]) == 12`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project statement on the vulnerable path that materializes the attacker-controlled coSWID `tag-id` text.
Root cause. The GUID section-length guard uses `&&` instead of `||`, so a candidate with only some malformed sections is accepted.
ASan crash site. The fixed 2-byte copy from the last GUID field reads past the heap string allocated for `split[4]`.

edges.evidence: The vulnerable original assertion trace records equal `last_field_ptr` values at `guid_section_guard` and the subsequent `guid_tail_copy` event. The adjacent `same_digits_valid_guid` perturbation records the same pointer equality on both vulnerable and fixed sides.
